Tax Deed Property Deals in Georgia: What Washington County Investors Need to Know

If you’re thinking about getting into real estate investing, Washington County, Georgia, might be a good place to start. When property owners don’t pay their property taxes, the county can auction those properties to recover the debt. These tax sales offer a chance to buy land or homes at below-market prices.

Let’s walk through everything you need to know, especially if this is your first time looking into tax deed investing in Washington County.

Overview: Georgia’s Tax Deed System

Georgia uses a redeemable tax deed system. When you buy a property at a tax sale, you don’t become the full owner immediately. The original owner has 1 year and 1 day to repay the amount you spent—plus a 20% penalty—to reclaim the property.

If they don’t pay within that window, you can file a quiet title action to claim full ownership.

Fun Facts About Georgia and Washington County

  • Georgia has 159 counties—second only to Texas.
  • Washington County was established in 1784 and named after George Washington.
  • The county seat, Sandersville, is often called the “Kaolin Capital of the World.”
  • Kaolin is a white clay used in paper, ceramics, and cosmetics. The mining industry supports a strong local job market.
  • Washington County’s low cost of living and rural setting attract first-time buyers and retirees alike.

Attractions and Local Highlights

Things to Do

  • Stroll through historic downtown Sandersville
  • Explore local parks, lakes, and nature trails
  • Visit the Washington County Historical Museum
  • Attend seasonal fairs and community events

Getting Around

  • Easy access to State Routes 15 and 24
  • Short drive to Macon and Augusta
  • Regional bus services and local highways connect the county to the rest of Georgia

Key Industries

  • Kaolin mining
  • Forestry and timber
  • Agriculture
  • Small manufacturing businesses

Community Life

  • Peaceful neighborhoods with affordable housing
  • Plenty of outdoor recreation like fishing, hunting, and hiking
  • Great for remote workers, retirees, and families looking for space and savings

Why Georgia Is a Great Place for Tax Deed Investors

Georgia’s system offers:

  • High returns – a guaranteed 20% if the property is redeemed
  • Low upfront costs – bidding starts at unpaid taxes
  • Fair risk – the redeemable deed process either returns your investment with interest or leads to full ownership
  • A clear auction system that’s open to anyone

How the Auction Process Works in Washington County

  1. Arrive early to register (starts at 9:00 AM)
  2. Bring a valid ID and certified funds
  3. Auction begins at 10:00 AM at the courthouse steps
  4. Bidding starts at the amount owed in taxes
  5. Highest bidder wins
  6. Pay in full within 1 hour
  7. Receive a Sheriff’s Tax Deed by mail

Expected Returns from Georgia Tax Deeds

  • Earn a minimum 20% return if the property is redeemed
  • Gain full ownership if it’s not redeemed within 1 year and 1 day
  • Potential for resale, rental income, or land development after gaining title

Can Foreign Investors Buy in Washington County?

Yes, both out-of-state and international buyers can bid and buy. Just make sure you or your legal rep can attend the sale in person.

Why Due Diligence Matters in Washington County

Before you buy:

  • Use plat maps to check property boundaries
  • Check if it’s in a historic zone (especially in Sandersville)
  • Visit the site (from the street) to assess location
  • Review any zoning rules
  • Search for existing liens or legal issues

Skipping due diligence could lead to buying land you can’t use or sell.

Can You Buy Over-the-Counter (OTC) in Washington County?

Yes. If a property isn’t sold at auction, it may become available over-the-counter.

Benefits of OTC purchases:

  • Fixed pricing
  • Less competition
  • More time to do research
  • Often simpler transactions

Check the Washington County Auction Calendar to see available properties.

Real Estate Trends in Washington County

  • Affordable land in rural areas offers long-term value
  • Historic homes in towns like Sandersville attract restoration buyers
  • Properties near mining jobs keep rental markets stable
  • Small-town charm and low property taxes appeal to newcomers

FAQs About Tax Deed Investing in Washington County, GA

Q: Can anyone attend the auction?
Yes. Bring your ID and certified funds to register.

Q: What if the owner pays back the taxes?
You’ll receive your bid amount back plus at least 20% interest.

Q: When do I get full ownership?
If the property isn’t redeemed after 1 year and 1 day, you can file for a quiet title.

Q: Are all liens wiped out?
Not necessarily. Always check for federal tax liens and other encumbrances.

Q: Do I need to inspect properties?
Yes. At least view them from the road, and check maps and legal records.

Pro Tips for First-Time Buyers

  • Research every parcel before you bid
  • Be ready to act fast—full payment is due within 1 hour
  • Stay away from landlocked or oddly shaped parcels
  • Use GSCCCA for deed and lien history
  • Hire a local real estate attorney for the quiet title process

Conclusion: A Smart Move for Property Investors

Washington County gives investors a unique chance to buy real estate at great prices. With high returns, a transparent process, and access to local and OTC properties, it’s a great location for anyone serious about building a property portfolio.

Just remember: do your homework before you bid, and follow the right legal steps afterward.
